title: The pressure of ministry
scripture_text: “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles. But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you “Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rebel against their parents and have them put to death. You will be hated by everyone because of me, but the one who stands firm to the end will be saved. When you are persecuted in one place, flee to another. Truly I tell you, you will not finish going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes. The student is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master. It is enough for students to be like their teachers, and servants like their masters. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household! So do not be afraid of them, for there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, or hidden that will not be made known. What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the roofs. Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, be afraid of the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell. Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground outside your Father’s care. And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So don’t be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. “Whoever acknowledges me before others, I will also acknowledge before my Father in heaven. But whoever disowns me before others, I will disown before my Father in heaven. Do not suppose that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword. For I have come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law—a man’s enemies will be the members of his own household. Anyone who loves their father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; anyone who loves their son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. Whoever does not take up their cross and follow me is not worthy of me. Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it. Anyone who welcomes you welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. Whoever welcomes a prophet as a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person as a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward. And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones who is my disciple, truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose their reward.”
devotional:
How can we cope with the pressure of ministry?

We need to realise that vulnerability is normal.

Jesus said, ‘I am sending you out as sheep among wolves. Sheep and wolves do not mix very well. As far as wolves are concerned, sheep are the under dog. Wolves frighten sheep. Jesus is saying here, the Ministry I am sending you to will give you good reason to fear, to feel out of your depth.

Over half the references to wolves in the bible refer to religious leaders who misuse their authority. This is a scary thought, most of the time wolves may be religious people. We can all make the mistake of trying to protect ourselves from feelings of wanting to be in control, we want to look strong, and we want to give the impression that we can cope. But Jesus is saying that the very thing you want to run away from is the very thing you need. Vulnerability is a gift from God; God designed us with a need to be vulnerable.

How can we live with feelings of vulnerability? Be shrewd and innocent.

Being shrewd and being innocent will never protect us from venerability, but it will help us to live with our vulnerability.

We need to notice that the emphasis of Jesus is not on some activity, or some course on self-protection against wolves. Rather his emphasis is on who we are.

Shrewd!

The Greek word Phronimos means intelligent, sensible, thoughtful, prudent. Judicious and wise. The way to handle vulnerability is not to try and run from it hoping it will go away, but to be wise. Wisdom is seeing life from Gods perspective. Jesus is saying that the only way a sheep can cope with life among the wolves is to be wise. One of the reasons why we find vulnerability difficult to live with, is because often we only see life through our own eyes, our world is restricted and small, but when we see our world through God’s eyes the wolves don’t look so big or fearful.

Innocent Akeraios means unmixed.

This word was used to describe wine that was never watered down. It was used to describe a loan where the interest was guaranteed.

The second things we need if we are going to cope in vulnerable is to make sure that there are no mixed motives in our hearts. This innocence in the result of freedom, if we have no hidden agenda, if we present the gospel as a gift, then there will be no mixed motives in our hearts.

When our motives are mixed and confused, then we are going to find it much more difficult to live with vulnerability. But if we live with a single eye on the purposes of God, then we will be more able to cope because we will have no hidden agenda to protect. Jesus is saying that being innocent and shrewd are not only the ways that we should respond to vulnerability, but they are also the means whereby we can live with our vulnerability. Wisdom and innocence cannot be self produced, they are the result of the work of God in someone’s heart. Being wise will protect your thinking, being innocent will protect your heart and motives.

In the face of severe vulnerability, it is easy for your thinking to become obsessive or irrational, or suspicious, or cynical. It is also easy for your heart to become hard, or insensitive feeling the need to bite back. Wise innocence is the only way we have of surviving the ministry Jesus has sent us to.

Being wise, and being innocent will affect how we see others. Being wise will make us cautious about how we see others, being innocent will prevent our caution from being tinged with suspicion.
prayer: Father thank you that often vulnerabilities are consistent with your will.
